title: Hibernate and JPA: object-relational mapping and the N+1 problem

videos.script: Lesson 9 wrote every SQL statement by hand. It read each column, and copied each row into a record. {{jdbc}} An object-relational mapper takes over that work. You describe a class, and Hibernate turns rows into objects, and changes into updates. {{mapping}} That saves a lot of typing. It also hides the SQL, and hidden SQL is where the surprises are. {{hidden}} In this lesson the bookshop's authors get a table of their own. Book and Author become entities, and an entity manager loads them. {{entities}} You change a price without calling save, and an update reaches the database anyway. {{dirty}} Then you ask for six books, and count the queries in the log. One for the books. One more for each author. That is the N+1 problem. {{count}} Two words in the query bring it down to a single statement. {{fetch}} And you meet the exception Hibernate throws when a lazy author is read too late, and the setting that hides it. {{lazy}}
